title: Cost meter — usage against the WEEKLY PLAN ALLOWANCE, plus per-lane dollars
note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-21: 'pace ourselves based on the weekly budget for the $200 Max plan -- 10% of the weekly budget a day, so we leave a wide margin for error or unexpected needs.' 10%/day x 7 = 70% of the weekly allowance, 30% margin. [!] THIS CHANGES WHAT THIS ITEM MEASURES AND THE CHANGE IS NOT COSMETIC. A subscription plan's constraint is a WEEKLY USAGE ALLOWANCE, not a dollar spend. Every cost_usd figure in the plan (the $125 across two resumed lanes, the $11.88 in ten minutes) is API-EQUIVALENT PRICING read off session metadata -- the right signal for COMPARING lanes, the wrong denominator for PACING against a plan. Report usage-against-allowance as the budget line, keep dollars beside it as the per-lane comparison. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the exact weekly allowance is not readable from this repo. FIRST JOB is to establish it from whatever surface reports plan usage, or from the operator, and to report `unknown` rather than substitute a figure until it has. A fabricated denominator under a real rule is worse than no meter. [!] THE DENOMINATOR IS ESTABLISHED 2026-09-21, AND IT IS A PERCENTAGE, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The operator read Settings > Usage directly. Plan: Max (20x). The surface exposes THREE meters, each a percent-of-allowance bar with no absolute number anywhere: a ~5-hour SESSION window, a WEEKLY window, and a SEPARATE WEEKLY LIMIT FOR FABLE. Anthropic's own support pages publish no figure either -- only '20x Pro per-session allowance'. [!] DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS, and this is a design decision rather than a limitation. The allowance is MODEL-WEIGHTED, so tokens-per-percent is not a constant -- it is a function of the model mix and moves whenever the manager routes a lane to sonnet instead of opus. A token budget would read as precise and drift silently. A1 METERS IN PERCENT. The operator's rule -- 10% of the weekly budget per day -- is already stated in that unit, so no conversion is needed to enforce it. A measured per-model exchange rate may be reported as a sanity check, labelled measured and drifting, NEVER as the budget. [!] TWO WINDOWS BIND, NOT ONE. The weekly cap is what the 10%/day rule governs; the ~5-hour session window is what actually walls a lane mid-run. A day's 10% spent as a single burst can exhaust the session window while the weekly meter still reads green, so A1 MUST SHOW BOTH or it reports 'fine' during an outage. [!] MEASURED 2026-09-21, and it CORRECTS an earlier claim on this row that was asserted rather than checked. The claim was that a meter summing only agent lanes would systematically under-report because the operator's own chat draws on the same pool. The mechanism is real -- all surfaces do share one limit -- but the magnitude is currently ZERO: 'What's using your week' reads Claude Code 100%, Chats 0%, Cowork 0%, Other 0%. Lane accounting is therefore ~= the whole pool today. A1 should still LABEL its scope, because the day that mix changes the meter goes quietly wrong. [!] THE MANAGER'S METER IS THE **DAILY** BUDGET, NOT THE WEEKLY BAR (operator, 2026-09-21): 'the manager should be focused on the daily budget, not weekly, as I sometimes use Claude for other projects... I will start a new manager session after this one and I expect it to use the daily budget, even if we pass into the margin.' [!] THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM WRITTEN ON THIS ROW EARLIER THE SAME DAY, and it is the SAME CATEGORY ERROR this row already caught once with cost_usd. That claim read: '68% of the week consumed with ~2 of 7 days left, ~13.6%/day against a 10%/day target, so THE STATED POLICY IS NOT BEING MET.' It compared TOTAL weekly consumption against the MANAGER'S daily allowance -- two different populations. The weekly bar aggregates every surface and every project the operator touches, including work this repo's manager cannot see and did not cause, so it CANNOT grade the manager. ('Claude Code 100%' does not rescue it: the operator's other projects are also Claude Code.) The 68% reading stands as a fact about the ACCOUNT; the conclusion drawn from it was unsupported and is withdrawn. [!] SO A1 REPORTS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND MUST NOT BLEND THEM. (a) THE CONTROL VARIABLE: this repo's spend today against the daily budget -- 10% of the weekly allowance. That is the number the manager is accountable for. (b) CONTEXT ONLY: the account-level weekly bar, unattributable and reported as such. A single blended 'budget' figure is the bug. [!] THE 30% WEEKLY MARGIN IS NOT A RESERVE THE MANAGER PRESERVES BY DOING LESS. It exists to absorb the operator's other projects and surprises. A manager that throttles its own lane because the ACCOUNT bar looks high is spending the margin's purpose on nothing. The operator has stated explicitly that the next manager should spend its daily budget EVEN IF that passes into the margin. [!] AND THE FAILURE MODE IS NOT HITTING A CAP -- it is 'losing work to sessions dying in the middle' (operator). THAT IS A DURABILITY PROBLEM, NOT A BUDGET ONE, and budgeting alone cannot fix it. The mitigations are structural: land work in small PRs rather than one large one, push before you answer, and keep state on disk (PIPELINE.jsonl, the checklist) rather than in a session's head. The ~5-HOUR SESSION WINDOW is what actually kills a session mid-task, so it is the in-session number to watch; the weekly bar never killed anything mid-run. [!] FABLE HAS A SEPARATE WEEKLY ALLOWANCE, MEASURED AT 0% USED, AND THE OPERATOR HAS DIRECTED THAT IT BE EMPLOYED (2026-09-21): 'it should definitely be used when appropriate -- we want to employ that budget as well, we just want to make sure it is getting the tasks that are the best use of that resource.' It is a SECOND pool that does not draw on the main one, so work routed there is additive capacity, not a trade-off. That makes it a live routing input for the model table in .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md. Tracked as E11 -- A1 reports the pool, E11 decides what goes in it. [!] DISPATCHED 2026-09-21 alongside A3a rather than before it, because A3a was told to render section 5 WITHOUT the spend figures (it already has the unrouted count from pipeline.py) and to print an explicit 'not measured -- A1 not built' line. So the blocked_on edge is narrower than it read: section 5 ships either way and A1 fills it in. FRESH, sonnet-5. [!] THE QUESTION PUT TO THE LANE is deliberately not 'build a cost meter' but 'what does section 5 print on a day nobody has read the usage meter' -- because the denominator is not machine-readable and the failure mode on this row has twice been a figure that looked precise and was not.
